(i) the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations for overdamped motion in nonlinear drag forces have an H theorem, (ii) they have exact solutions of the form of stretched q-exponential distributions, (iii) these solutions are stable, in the sense that the evolution equation preserves the q-exponential functional form of the distribution.
the thermostatistics of interacting particles performing nonlinear overdamped motion is governed by nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, and that these equations have stretched q exponential solutions.

the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation with the nonlinear drag force is a nontrivial generalization of the linear Fokker- Planck equation and the nonlinear Fokler-Planck equation is a nontrivail generalization of the Boltzmann equation.

the effects of nonlinear friction on the statistical mechanics of overdamped systems.
the statistical physics of overdamped motion with nonlinear friction.
the effects of nonlinear friction on the statistical mechanics of systems of particles performing overdamped dynamics.

nonlinear drag forces are an important and relevant phenomenon in the dynamics of interacting particles performing Brownian motion.
the nonlinearities in the drag force lead to a more rapid approach to the equilibrium state, as measured by the time required for a system to reach a state of maximum entropy.

nonlinear drag forces are able to generate stretched exponentials as the steady state distribution of the systems under study.

nonlinear drag forces can lead to the emergence of stretched exponential relaxation, which is an important feature of the nonequilibrium dynamics of a wide variety of systems.
